text:
Site A "Brookfield": Franklin County, PA. 100 MW solar + 50 MW storage, target COD 2030. Former industrial land we control, already zoned industrial. Substation is 1.5 miles away on our own land (1 parcel). No wetlands, no homes nearby, no objections we know of.
Site B "Ridgeview": Sussex County, VA. 100 MW solar + 50 MW storage, COD 2030. Greenfield farmland next to a subdivision. Gen-tie route is 6 miles across 4 parcels. No wetlands mapped. Neighbors objected to another solar farm at a county hearing last year.
Site C "Meadow Creek": Clinton County, OH. 100 MW solar + 50 MW storage, COD 2030. Greenfield near a creek with a mapped wetland crossing. Connection route not confirmed yet. Homes nearby unknown.

site.name: Brookfield
site.notes: Controlled former industrial land, zoned industrial; substation is on the same land.

drivers.label: Restudy allocation watch
drivers.reason: Spread of 1.5 warrants watch; county withdrawals below state rate.

drivers.label: Short direct route
drivers.reason: 1.5 miles and one parcel to cross.

drivers.label: Industrial zoning fit
drivers.reason: Former industrial, industrial-zoned land lowers siting risk.

drivers.label: No reported opposition
drivers.reason: No nearby homes or local objections reported.

result.summary: No statewide siting authority for solar. Municipal zoning ordinances decide where projects can go. Construction disturbing 1+ acre needs a DEP NPDES stormwater permit.

site.name: Ridgeview
site.notes: Greenfield farmland next to a subdivision; neighbors objected to another solar farm at a county hearing last year.

drivers.label: High upgrade exposure
drivers.reason: County studies ranked at the 92nd percentile of the pool.

drivers.label: Shared upgrade risk
drivers.reason: Two shared substations and high activity increase restudy allocation risk.

drivers.label: Local approval scrutiny
drivers.reason: Farmland faces local zoning approval under a local-veto regime.

drivers.label: Neighbor opposition
drivers.reason: Local objections are reported near homes.

result.summary: Local zoning approval (conditional or special use permit) plus a comprehensive-plan review are required. Localities can negotiate siting agreements. State DEQ Permit by Rule covers solar up to 150 MW.

site.name: Meadow Creek
site.notes: Near a creek with a mapped wetland crossing; connection route not confirmed.

drivers.label: Limited County Evidence
drivers.reason: One county study limits confidence; Dayton’s median is below the pool median.

drivers.label: Restudy Exposure
drivers.reason: One shared substation reaches 300 active megawatts; county withdrawals were 100%.

drivers.label: Route Unconfirmed
drivers.reason: Distance and parcel crossings are unknown; connection route remains unconfirmed.

drivers.label: Wetland And Siting
drivers.reason: Wetlands are present; large solar faces county-ban authority under Ohio rules.

drivers.label: Community Unknown
drivers.reason: Nearby homes and local objections are unknown; missing records do not show support.

card.next_action: Confirm route and wetland impacts first

result.summary: Projects of 50 MW or more need an OPSB certificate. Under SB 52 (2021), county commissioners can ban large solar in unincorporated areas and sit on the OPSB panel for the case.

portfolio.headline: Prioritize Brookfield; Meadow Creek ranks ahead of Ridgeview on fewer higher-risk ratings.
